pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Async imports of all apps
pr.title: Async import of the appStore packages

raw_findings.body: Every `import("./<app>")` expression is executed while the object literal is constructed, so all ~28 app packages are still resolved and evaluated at module-evaluation time; the stated goal of async/lazy app loading is not achieved and startup cost is unchanged (now with extra promise overhead).
raw_findings.failure_mode: The intended lazy-loading behavior silently does not happen; all app modules load regardless of which one is needed.
raw_findings.impact: Every `import("./<app>")` expression is executed while the object literal is constructed, so all ~28 app packages are still resolved and evaluated at module-evaluation time; the stated goal of async/lazy app loading is not achieved and startup cost is unchanged (now with extra promise overhead).
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor replaced static `import * as x` with immediately-evaluated `import(...)` expressions inside an object literal rather than lazily-invoked import factories.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Store thunks instead of promises, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and invoke the thunk at the lookup sites (`await appStore[key]()`).
raw_findings.title: Dynamic imports in appStore are invoked eagerly, so no app is loaded lazily
raw_findings.trigger: Any module importing `@calcom/app-store` (e.g. `packages/core/videoClient.ts`, `packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts`) is evaluated, for example on the first booking request in a serverless function.

raw_findings.body: The rejected promise stored in the `appStore` object is never awaited by any code path, producing an unhandled promise rejection which terminates the Node process by default on Node >= 15 instead of failing only the one unusable app.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A single broken app module turns from a localized `is not implemented` warning into a process-wide unhandled rejection.
raw_findings.impact: The rejected promise stored in the `appStore` object is never awaited by any code path, producing an unhandled promise rejection which terminates the Node process by default on Node >= 15 instead of failing only the one unusable app.
raw_findings.root_cause: All dynamic import promises are created at module-evaluation time while only the looked-up key is ever awaited, leaving the other promises without a rejection handler.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the entries lazy factories (`() => import("./closecom")`) so a promise is only created — and therefore always awaited — when that specific app is requested.
raw_findings.title: Eagerly created app import promises can become unhandled rejections
raw_findings.trigger: One app module fails to evaluate or its chunk fails to load (throwing module-level initialization, missing optional dependency, chunk-load failure) while the request only awaits a different app key such as `googlecalendar`.

raw_findings.body: The path lost its underscore prefix, so uncommenting resolves to a directory that does not exist and produces a module-not-found build error instead of a working template.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The template comment misleads contributors into referencing a path that cannot resolve.
raw_findings.impact: The path lost its underscore prefix, so uncommenting resolves to a directory that does not exist and produces a module-not-found build error instead of a working template.
raw_findings.root_cause: The comment was rewritten by hand during the conversion to dynamic imports and dropped the `_` prefix of the `_example` folder.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original directory name in the comment: `// example: import("./_example"),`.
raw_findings.title: Commented-out example entry points at a non-existent "./example" path
raw_findings.trigger: A developer follows the in-file template and uncomments the line to register a new app, as the previous comment (`import * as example from "./_example";`) instructed.

raw_findings.body: `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the returned promise, so the rejection is no longer caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }`; it becomes an unhandled rejection, and `Reschedule` continues (sending emails and returning true) before any calendar event deletion has been attempted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Errors are silently lost and calendar deletions are not guaranteed to complete before the handler returns.
raw_findings.impact: `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the returned promise, so the rejection is no longer caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }`; it becomes an unhandled rejection, and `Reschedule` continues (sending emails and returning true) before any calendar event deletion has been attempted.
raw_findings.root_cause: Making `getCalendar` asynchronous forced the callback to be `async`, but the iteration construct was left as `forEach`, which neither awaits nor propagates the returned promise.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `forEach` with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` (or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`) inside the existing try block.
raw_findings.title: async forEach callback escapes the surrounding try/catch in vital reschedule
raw_findings.trigger: A reschedule request where `getCalendar` rejects (for example the dynamic app import fails or the credential type is unsupported and the awaited import throws) for one of the booking references.

raw_findings.body: The promise returned by the async callback is discarded by `forEach`, so the enclosing `try/catch` no longer logs the error; the rejection surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the deletion of the old calendar event may never run before the function returns true.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error handling added around this block becomes dead code and cancellation work is fire-and-forget.
raw_findings.impact: The promise returned by the async callback is discarded by `forEach`, so the enclosing `try/catch` no longer logs the error; the rejection surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the deletion of the old calendar event may never run before the function returns true.
raw_findings.root_cause: The callback was converted to `async` to await the now-asynchronous `getCalendar` without changing the non-awaiting `forEach` iteration.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Iterate with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered)` and `await` each branch inside the existing try block, or `await Promise.all(...map(async ...))`.
raw_findings.title: async forEach callback escapes the surrounding try/catch in wipemycalother reschedule
raw_findings.trigger: A reschedule request where the awaited `getCalendar(...)` rejects for one of the filtered booking references (failed app import or throwing calendar service constructor).

raw_findings.body: Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` propagated out of the tRPC procedure and surfaced as a request error; now the rejection is swallowed by `forEach` into an unhandled promise rejection while the mutation continues to send reschedule emails and webhooks as if the calendar cleanup succeeded.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Calendar deletion failures are no longer observable and are not awaited before the mutation resolves.
raw_findings.impact: Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` propagated out of the tRPC procedure and surfaced as a request error; now the rejection is swallowed by `forEach` into an unhandled promise rejection while the mutation continues to send reschedule emails and webhooks as if the calendar cleanup succeeded.
raw_findings.root_cause: Awaiting the newly asynchronous `getCalendar` inside a `forEach` callback detaches the resulting promise from the procedure's control flow.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Convert the loop to `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` (the enclosing procedure is already async) so failures propagate to the caller.
raw_findings.title: async forEach in requestReschedule drops getCalendar rejections
raw_findings.trigger: A `requestReschedule` mutation where `await getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type))` rejects (dynamic app import failure or a throwing CalendarService constructor).

raw_findings.body: The item's `calendar` property silently changed type from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>` while `getCalendarCredentials` stayed synchronous; the promise is created eagerly per credential and only awaited here, so an unused/filtered-out item's rejection is never handled and any direct method call on `calendar` fails.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An exported helper's documented return shape changes implicitly, so other consumers receive a promise where an object is expected.
raw_findings.impact: The item's `calendar` property silently changed type from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>` while `getCalendarCredentials` stayed synchronous; the promise is created eagerly per credential and only awaited here, so an unused/filtered-out item's rejection is never handled and any direct method call on `calendar` fails.
raw_findings.root_cause: `getCalendar` became asynchronous but the call site at `getCalendarCredentials` was left un-awaited, with the await pushed into one particular consumer.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make `getCalendarCredentials` async and `await getCalendar(credential)` there (updating callers), instead of leaking a pending promise through its public return type.
raw_findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns unresolved calendar promises from a synchronous exported function
raw_findings.trigger: Any consumer of the exported `getCalendarCredentials(...)` other than `getConnectedCalendars` (e.g. `apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer.tsx`, or downstream API packages) reading the `calendar` field of a returned item.

raw_findings.body: The documented two-step registration (top-level `import * as x` plus adding the identifier) no longer matches the file, which now expects a single `name: import("./name")` entry; contributors add a static import that is inconsistent with the async lookup (`await appStore[key]`).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation describes a registration pattern that no longer exists in the changed file.
raw_findings.impact: The documented two-step registration (top-level `import * as x` plus adding the identifier) no longer matches the file, which now expects a single `name: import("./name")` entry; contributors add a static import that is inconsistent with the async lookup (`await appStore[key]`).
raw_findings.root_cause: The registration convention in `packages/app-store/index.ts` was changed without updating the developer documentation that describes it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update `apps/docs/pages/developer/app-store.mdx` to describe adding `yourapp: import("./yourapp")` to the `appStore` object in the same commit.
raw_findings.title: App-store registration docs are stale after the switch to dynamic imports
raw_findings.trigger: A contributor follows `apps/docs/pages/developer/app-store.mdx:43` ("Under `packages/app-store/index.ts`, import your app and add it under `appStore`") when adding a new app after this change.

validated_findings.impact: The path lost its underscore prefix, so uncommenting resolves to a directory that does not exist and produces a module-not-found build error instead of a working template.
validated_findings.root_cause: The comment was rewritten by hand during the conversion to dynamic imports and dropped the `_` prefix of the `_example` folder.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original directory name in the comment: `// example: import("./_example"),`.
validated_findings.title: Commented-out example entry points at a non-existent "./example" path
validated_findings.trigger: A developer follows the in-file template and uncomments the line to register a new app, as the previous comment (`import * as example from "./_example";`) instructed.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R2 shows `// example: import("./example")`. The original code used `import * as example from "./_example"` (underscore prefix). The comment now references `./example` which does not exist; uncommenting would cause module-not-found error. Low severity but valid doc defect introduced by patch.

validated_findings.body: `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the returned promise, so the rejection is no longer caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }`; it becomes an unhandled rejection, and `Reschedule` continues (sending emails and returning true) before any calendar event deletion has been attempted.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Errors are silently lost and calendar deletions are not guaranteed to complete before the handler returns.
validated_findings.impact: `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the returned promise, so the rejection is no longer caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }`; it becomes an unhandled rejection, and `Reschedule` continues (sending emails and returning true) before any calendar event deletion has been attempted.
validated_findings.root_cause: Making `getCalendar` asynchronous forced the callback to be `async`, but the iteration construct was left as `forEach`, which neither awaits nor propagates the returned promise.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `forEach` with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` (or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`) inside the existing try block.
validated_findings.title: async forEach callback escapes the surrounding try/catch in vital reschedule
validated_findings.trigger: A reschedule request where `getCalendar` rejects (for example the dynamic app import fails or the credential type is unsupported and the awaited import throws) for one of the booking references.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows line R125 changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {`. forEach ignores returned promises, so async callback's rejection escapes the try/catch at L124. The function returns true before deletions complete. Concrete bug introduced by patch.

validated_findings.body: The promise returned by the async callback is discarded by `forEach`, so the enclosing `try/catch` no longer logs the error; the rejection surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the deletion of the old calendar event may never run before the function returns true.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Error handling added around this block becomes dead code and cancellation work is fire-and-forget.
validated_findings.impact: The promise returned by the async callback is discarded by `forEach`, so the enclosing `try/catch` no longer logs the error; the rejection surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the deletion of the old calendar event may never run before the function returns true.
validated_findings.root_cause: The callback was converted to `async` to await the now-asynchronous `getCalendar` without changing the non-awaiting `forEach` iteration.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Iterate with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered)` and `await` each branch inside the existing try block, or `await Promise.all(...map(async ...))`.
validated_findings.title: async forEach callback escapes the surrounding try/catch in wipemycalother reschedule
validated_findings.trigger: A reschedule request where the awaited `getCalendar(...)` rejects for one of the filtered booking references (failed app import or throwing calendar service constructor).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Identical pattern to candidate 3 but in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125. Same causal defect (async forEach), same fix. Merge into candidate 3 as canonical.

validated_findings.body: Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` propagated out of the tRPC procedure and surfaced as a request error; now the rejection is swallowed by `forEach` into an unhandled promise rejection while the mutation continues to send reschedule emails and webhooks as if the calendar cleanup succeeded.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Calendar deletion failures are no longer observable and are not awaited before the mutation resolves.
validated_findings.impact: Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` propagated out of the tRPC procedure and surfaced as a request error; now the rejection is swallowed by `forEach` into an unhandled promise rejection while the mutation continues to send reschedule emails and webhooks as if the calendar cleanup succeeded.
validated_findings.root_cause: Awaiting the newly asynchronous `getCalendar` inside a `forEach` callback detaches the resulting promise from the procedure's control flow.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Convert the loop to `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` (the enclosing procedure is already async) so failures propagate to the caller.
validated_findings.title: async forEach in requestReschedule drops getCalendar rejections
validated_findings.trigger: A `requestReschedule` mutation where `await getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type))` rejects (dynamic app import failure or a throwing CalendarService constructor).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R553 shows `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` in bookings.tsx. Same async forEach pattern but different file (tRPC router) and no surrounding try/catch at all. Independently fixable site from candidates 3/4. Calendar deletions fire-and-forget before mutation resolves.

validated_findings.body: The item's `calendar` property silently changed type from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>` while `getCalendarCredentials` stayed synchronous; the promise is created eagerly per credential and only awaited here, so an unused/filtered-out item's rejection is never handled and any direct method call on `calendar` fails.
validated_findings.failure_mode: An exported helper's documented return shape changes implicitly, so other consumers receive a promise where an object is expected.
validated_findings.impact: The item's `calendar` property silently changed type from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>` while `getCalendarCredentials` stayed synchronous; the promise is created eagerly per credential and only awaited here, so an unused/filtered-out item's rejection is never handled and any direct method call on `calendar` fails.
validated_findings.root_cause: `getCalendar` became asynchronous but the call site at `getCalendarCredentials` was left un-awaited, with the await pushed into one particular consumer.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Make `getCalendarCredentials` async and `await getCalendar(credential)` there (updating callers), instead of leaking a pending promise through its public return type.
validated_findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns unresolved calendar promises from a synchronous exported function
validated_findings.trigger: Any consumer of the exported `getCalendarCredentials(...)` other than `getConnectedCalendars` (e.g. `apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer.tsx`, or downstream API packages) reading the `calendar` field of a returned item.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows getCalendarCredentials (L28) calls `getCalendar(credential)` which is now async, storing a Promise in `calendar` property. The function remains synchronous, returning items with unresolved promises. Line R48 shows `await item.calendar` in getConnectedCalendars. Other consumers may not await. Type silently changed from Calendar|null to Promise<Calendar|null>.

validated_findings.body: The documented two-step registration (top-level `import * as x` plus adding the identifier) no longer matches the file, which now expects a single `name: import("./name")` entry; contributors add a static import that is inconsistent with the async lookup (`await appStore[key]`).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Documentation describes a registration pattern that no longer exists in the changed file.
validated_findings.impact: The documented two-step registration (top-level `import * as x` plus adding the identifier) no longer matches the file, which now expects a single `name: import("./name")` entry; contributors add a static import that is inconsistent with the async lookup (`await appStore[key]`).
validated_findings.root_cause: The registration convention in `packages/app-store/index.ts` was changed without updating the developer documentation that describes it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update `apps/docs/pages/developer/app-store.mdx` to describe adding `yourapp: import("./yourapp")` to the `appStore` object in the same commit.
validated_findings.title: App-store registration docs are stale after the switch to dynamic imports
validated_findings.trigger: A contributor follows `apps/docs/pages/developer/app-store.mdx:43` ("Under `packages/app-store/index.ts`, import your app and add it under `appStore`") when adding a new app after this change.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Claim about stale documentation in apps/docs/pages/developer/app-store.mdx is not grounded in the patch or provided context. No evidence the documentation file exists or what it says. The finding speculates about external docs without concrete proof.
